text: A lambda is a tiny, anonymous function you can write in a single line, with no name and no def keyword.
The word lambda, then the parameters, a colon, and one expression whose value is returned automatically.
So square of five gives twenty-five, and add of three and seven gives ten — just like regular functions.
[chuckle] But you rarely name a lambda like this — their real power is being passed straight into another function.
Here we hand a lambda to map, squaring every number in the list without ever defining a separate function.
[sigh] Lambdas are perfect as a sort key too — this one tells sort to order the pairs by their second element.
So the tuples rearrange alphabetically by their letter, not by their number.
A lambda can even hold a conditional expression, returning pass or fail depending on the score.
[groan] Keep them short though — if a lambda gets complicated, a normal named function is always the clearer choice.
